A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CHIPS. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I are readable and matchable despite reflow and equation renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-pretraining evaluations, cross-backbone experiments, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2–4 and the MedTrinity experiments in Tables 34–35.

M1.justification: The endpoint-subspace alignment, positive/negative curvature mixing, JL sketching, learnability and relevance weights, and top-n selection remain unchanged. Appendix C and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both use BIOMEDICA and MedTrinity and the same medical and general-domain classification/retrieval benchmarks. The additional MedTrinity results in Appendix I already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: Random, Concept-Balance, Concept-Filter, CLIPScore, Dot, TracIn, and TRAK, with the same specialized medical CLIP references. Comparator membership in the generalization and ablation experiments also matches.

E3.justification: Model configurations, retention budgets, five-epoch AdamW training, global batch size of 32,768, accuracy/R@1 metrics, and sensitivity-test settings are unchanged. The beta grid omitted from v2's prose remains documented in Figure 2 and the appendix.

E4.justification: Both retain identical component ablations, evaluation-set-size and alpha/beta sweeps, endpoint-subspace comparisons, random-projection analyses, and score distributions, including their detailed appendix results.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1 retains the same seed-fixing and determinism disclosures. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, empirical confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and findings are unchanged, including Table 2 medical averages of 27.03, 28.20, and 29.96, the proxy/full Spearman correlation of 0.83, and all detailed results in Appendices H–I.

T1.justification: Section 2.4 removes the reweighted-distribution definitions, density-ratio bound, and derivation of KL divergence at most 1 nat, replacing them with qualitative prose. This argument is not relocated to the appendices. The two main theorems and Appendix B proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the explicit 10–30% restriction on the general-retention claim with 'all retention ratios,' making it less qualified without new evidence. The conclusion still specifies 10–30%; the principal method and data-efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 explicitly explains why Spearman correlation matters for sample ranking. The introduction also recasts endpoint dominance from an argument about early-stage parameter updates to one about full-parameter influence computation. The target-validation limitation and main adaptation–retention interpretation remain.

D1.justification: v1's promise to release code, data, and checkpoints is removed, while v2 adds a GitHub repository footnote. This supplies access information, although the PDFs do not establish repository contents or availability. Implementation and hardware disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and Appendix A research positioning are unchanged. Edits to references [20] and [46] concern bibliographic metadata rather than added or removed works.

P1.justification: The contribution bullets become a paragraph, Section 2.2 is rewritten to explain local maps and residuals, and surrounding prose is tightened. The section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 are resized and repositioned, text and float spacing change, the conclusion moves onto page 8, and printed page numbers disappear. The same figures and tables remain, with unchanged plotted evidence and table structures.

improvement.justification: Clearer explanations and a repository link offer limited benefits, but v2 weakens theoretical traceability: it removes the explicit drift argument while retaining bounded-drift assertions, and Section 2.2 points to Appendix B.2 for preconditioning transformations that the unchanged appendix does not supply. The abstract also loses an explicit scope restriction. These are modest losses of precision; the method and empirical evidence remain intact.
